newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DJORKAEFF PENALTY SEES FRANCE TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DJORKAEFF PENALTY SEES FRANCE TO VICTORY.

text.p: France recorded an unconvincing 1-0 victory over Sweden at the Parc des Princes on Wednesday in their last friendly before launching their campaign for the 1998 World Cup.
A penalty by Internazionale striker Youri Djorkaeff shortly before the break was all the French could manage as they put on another lacklustre performance in front of goal.
The result was all the more fortunate as the penalty, awarded by Belgian referee Markus Sandra for a foul on Djorkaeff by Sweden's veteran goalkeeper Thomas Ravelli, looked very generous.
Otherwise, the best chances on a warm night in Paris fell to the Swedes.

Martin Dahlin had a fine opportunity to open the scoring with a header in the 20th minute and goalkeeper Fabien Barthez twice had to intervene at the feet of Kennet Anderson after blunders in his defence.
France manager Aime Jacquet has had problems in attack since his side lost in the semifinals of the European championship last June.
He has not found the answers yet ahead of next June's Tournoi de France, involving Brazil, England and Italy.
"It was not a great night for us. Our performance was pedestrian," Jacquet admitted.
"We lacked pace and will. It's probably one of the worst matches I've seen us play."
The pairing of Djorkaeff and Juventus playmaker Zinedine Zidane again proved ineffective as Djorkaeff was barely involved before plunging into the box in the 44th minue to secure a penalty.
Zidane was replaced by Franck Gava in the 57th minute. Jacquet made four other substitutions in the second half but to no effect.
Sweden, by contrast, looked in reasonable shape ahead of their crucial World Cup qualifier against Scotland on April 30.
Kennet Andersson appeared to have recovered some of the poise which made him one of the best strikers of the 1994 World Cup finals while the defence was very solid.
